title: Who may issue a Schedule III through VI prescription fillable under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c)
subtopic: Out-of-state Schedule III through VI issuing conditions
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c) a prescription for a controlled substance contained in SCHEDULES III TO VI, INCLUSIVE, as defined in section 3, may also be issued by an authorized practitioner who is DULY LICENSED AND AUTHORIZED TO ENGAGE IN PRESCRIPTIVE PRACTICE and DULY REGISTERED IN THE STATE WHEREIN HE RESIDES, IF REQUIRED, and DULY REGISTERED UNDER FEDERAL LAW TO WRITE PRESCRIPTIONS. That wording differs from s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2), which speak of registration in another state where the practitioner RESIDES OR PRACTICES, if required. The paragraph is VALID ONLY FOR THE PURPOSE OF AUTHORIZING THE FILLING OF PRESCRIPTIONS, ISSUED WITHIN THE PRECEDING THIRTY DAYS, and shall not authorize the practitioner to process, administer or dispense controlled substances as provided in section 9 or to practice within the commonwealth. A prescription issued under the paragraph SHALL BE ISSUED IN THE MANNER PRESCRIBED IN SECTION 22, and all relevant provisions of chapter 94C apply to the practitioner and the prescription. Nothing contained in section 18 shall be deemed to authorize any mail order pharmacies.
exam_relevance: Tests the issuing condition s. 18(c) states in its own words, including the federal-registration condition it attaches to every prescription the paragraph reaches, Schedule VI included, and the thirty-day limit on what the paragraph authorizes.

numeric_facts.fact: Window of the filling authorization in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c)
numeric_facts.conditions: The paragraph authorizes the filling of prescriptions issued within the preceding thirty days

exceptions: The state-registration condition applies 'if required', so a practitioner whose state of residence does not require registration meets it without one; the federal-registration condition carries no such qualifier.
A practitioner authorized to prescribe controlled substances and registered under chapter 94C issues under s. 18(a), and s. 18(c) is not the authority for that prescription.
common_confusions: Carrying the 'resides or practices' wording of s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2) into s. 18(c), which speaks of the state wherein the practitioner resides.
Dropping the federal-registration condition, which s. 18(c) attaches to every prescription the paragraph reaches, Schedule VI included.
Reading the thirty days as a validity period for the prescription itself rather than as the limit on what s. 18(c) authorizes a pharmacist to fill.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c), read with the first sentences of s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2), read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
